wiki_catalogs.name: System Overview
wiki_catalogs.prompt: Create comprehensive content for the System Overview section focused on the Thumbnail Maker Studio. Explain its purpose as an AI-powered YouTube thumbnail generation and editing platform with social sharing, analytics, and collaboration features. Describe the full-stack architecture using React, Express, TypeScript, Prisma ORM, and Vite. Document the core user workflows from registration to thumbnail creation, editing, sharing, and performance tracking. Include high-level diagrams illustrating the system context, component interactions, and data flow between frontend, backend, database, and external services. Provide integration points with social media platforms and AI services. Highlight key technical decisions such as JWT authentication, RESTful API design, and monorepo structure. Include practical examples of common use cases and reference the project roadmap and glossary for context.

wiki_catalogs.name: UI Component Library
wiki_catalogs.prompt: Create detailed documentation for the UI Component Library used in Thumbnail Maker Studio. Describe each reusable component (Button, Card, Input, Panel, Toolbar, Slider, StatCard) including their visual design, behavior, and accessibility features. Document the available props, events, and styling customization options through CSS modules and the design system. Include code examples demonstrating usage in various contexts such as forms, dashboards, and modals. Explain the export mechanism via index.ts and type definitions in types.ts. Address responsive design considerations, theming support via CSS variables, and integration with the global dark mode. Provide guidelines for extending existing components or creating new ones while maintaining consistency with the design system.

wiki_catalogs.name: AI Enhancement Service
wiki_catalogs.prompt: Develop detailed content for the AI Enhancement Service, focusing on its implementation of style transfer and image enhancement using TensorFlow.js and Sharp. Document the available artistic styles (Impressionist, Cubist, Expressionist, Surrealist, Pop Art) and enhancement types (Super-resolution, Denoise, Deblur, Color Enhance, Sharpen). Include code examples showing the integration between AI and traditional processing methods, tensor manipulation, and image buffer handling. Describe the service's error handling, memory management with tensor disposal, and performance considerations for CPU-intensive operations. Address common issues such as model loading failures and provide troubleshooting guidance for degraded performance.

Document the ThemeToggle component’s role in user interaction and state persistence using localStorage. Include code examples demonstrating theme-aware component rendering and style composition. Address accessibility compliance (contrast ratios), performance implications of dynamic styling, and alignment with the Project Style Guide.md. Include data structures for advanced analytics features such as heatmaps, audience demographics, and platform-specific performance. Provide examples for retrieving CTR trends and tracking real-time engagement. Explain integration with AnalyticsDashboard.tsx and AdvancedAnalyticsDashboard.tsx components. Address data privacy considerations, sampling strategies for large datasets, and caching mechanisms for performance optimization.

wiki_catalogs.name: Pre-commit Quality Enforcement

Explain the Husky and lint-staged integration configured in package.json that automatically runs quality checks before each commit. Document the prepare script that installs Husky, the lint-staged configuration that applies ESLint and Prettier to staged TypeScript/TSX files (both root and client), and JSON/MD formatting. Describe the development workflow where developers run npm run check (format + lint) before committing, and how the pre-commit hook enforces code standards by running npx lint-staged and npm run test. Include practical examples from package.json and DEVELOPMENT_WORKFLOW.md, demonstrate the commit process with conventional commits via npm run commit, and address common issues like formatting failures or test breaks during pre-commit. Provide troubleshooting guidance and best practices for maintaining code quality at commit time.

Explain how Jest's moduleNameMapper is used to mock CSS imports and other static assets. Detail the use of ts-jest for transforming TypeScript files in both frontend and backend environments. Describe custom test utilities for setting up authenticated sessions, mocking Prisma repositories, and simulating external API responses (e.g., social media clients). wiki_catalogs.name: Batch Image Processing

<blog>
# Thumbnail Maker Studio: Comprehensive Project Overview

## 1. Project Introduction

### Purpose Statement
Thumbnail Maker Studio is an AI-powered application designed to help content creators generate professional, click-worthy YouTube thumbnails in seconds. The platform leverages artificial intelligence to analyze video content and automatically create optimized thumbnail designs that maximize viewer engagement and click-through rates.

### Core Goals and Objectives
- Enable creators to generate high-quality thumbnails without design expertise
- Automate thumbnail creation process using AI analysis of video content
- Provide advanced editing tools for customization
- Support social media sharing and analytics integration
- Offer scalable subscription-based access to thumbnail generation credits

### Target Audience
The primary users of this application are YouTube content creators, digital marketers, and social media managers who need to produce multiple high-performing thumbnails regularly. The platform caters to both individual creators and teams through collaboration features.

## 2. Technical Architecture

### Component Breakdown
The project follows a monorepo structure with a clear separation between frontend and backend components. It implements a modern full-stack architecture with React for the frontend, Express.js for the backend API, and Prisma for database management.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[Client] --> B[API Layer]
    B --> C[Business Logic]
    C --> D[Data Access]
    D --> E[(Database)]
    C --> F[AI Services]
    C --> G[Image Processing]
    H[Frontend] --> I[React Components]
    I --> J[State Management]
    J --> K[Context API]
```

### Design Patterns
The application employs several architectural patterns:
- **Modular Architecture**: Backend functionality is organized into distinct modules (auth, thumbnail, analytics, etc.)
- **RESTful API Design**: Clear endpoint structure with resource-based routing
- **Context API**: React Context for global state management (authentication, theme)
- **Service Pattern**: Business logic separated into service classes
- **Middleware Pattern**: Express middleware for authentication and request processing

### System Relationships
The system consists of interconnected components that communicate through well-defined interfaces. The frontend interacts with the backend via REST APIs, while the backend integrates with external services for AI processing and social media sharing.

```mermaid
graph TD
    Frontend[React Frontend] --> Backend[Express API]
    Backend --> Database[(Prisma/PostgreSQL)]
    Backend --> AI[TensorFlow AI Services]
    Backend --> ImageProcessing[Sharp Image Processing]
    Backend --> SocialMedia[Facebook, Twitter, LinkedIn, Pinterest]
    Frontend --> CloudStorage[S3/Cloud Storage]
```

### Data Flow
The application follows a unidirectional data flow pattern where user actions trigger API calls, which are processed by controllers, services, and data access layers before returning responses to the frontend.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    User[User Action] --> Frontend[React Component]
    Frontend --> API[API Call]
    API --> Controller[Controller]
    Controller --> Service[Service Layer]
    Service --> Repository[Repository/Prisma]
    Repository --> Database[(Database)]
    Database --> Repository
    Repository --> Service
    Service --> Controller
    Controller --> API
    API --> Frontend
    Frontend --> User[Updated UI]
```

## 3. Key Implementation

### Main Entry Points
- Frontend: `client/src/index.tsx` - React application entry point
- Backend: `src/server.ts` - Express server initialization

### Functionality Overview
The application provides a comprehensive suite of thumbnail creation and management features:

- AI-powered thumbnail generation from video links
- Advanced editing tools with layers and effects
- Template marketplace for pre-designed layouts
- Batch editing capabilities
- Social sharing analytics
- Team collaboration features
- User settings and preferences

### Implementation Highlights
The landing page serves as the primary user entry point, featuring a clean interface for video link input and thumbnail generation. The authentication system provides standard register/login functionality with password recovery.

The application supports both public and private thumbnail sharing with access controls, and provides detailed analytics on thumbnail performance across different platforms.
